answer: The switch is `SB_DISABLE_SERVICE_WORKER`. The memory only says it keeps online-only mode (no service worker) deliberately available. Online-only mode has no offline support and needs a network round-trip on every operation. The memory doesn't spell out the sync behavior beyond that.

### Decision

# Decision
v2 **eliminates the server-side PlugOS runtime**: plug execution, indexing, the query engine, [[Space Lua]], page rendering, and the [[Sync|sync engine]] now run **only in the client**. In effect, **sync mode becomes the only mode**, and the **server is reduced to a file store** — it lists, reads, writes and deletes files, handles authentication, serves the static client, and runs shell commands. See [[Architecture]].

--- [vault:corpus/docs/TLS.md] ---
### Untitled

#getting-started

While silverBullet works over plain HTTP on a LAN IP or hostname in online-only mode, _HTTPS_ enables the full feature set, including offline use and local encryption. This page documents a few deployment options.

> **note** Note
> This is a browser enforced restriction: browsers restrict service workers, crypto, and programmatic clipboard access to secure contexts. This is why the recommended deployment model is TLS, but SilverBullet will make a best effort to work without it.

--- [vault:corpus/docs/ADR/001 Offline-First PWA.md] ---
### Alternatives considered

# Alternatives considered
* **Online-only (no service worker).** Rejected: no offline support and a network round-trip on every operation — defeats the offline-first goal. (Still available deliberately via `SB_DISABLE_SERVICE_WORKER`.)
* **Bundle a native runtime for offline.** Rejected: heavier and platform-specific. A PWA delivers offline on every platform from one codebase.

--- [vault:corpus/docs/ADR/007 Core Application Logic on the Client.md] ---
### Alternatives considered

# Alternatives considered
* **Keep the dual-mode (server + sync) architecture.** Rejected: maintaining two PlugOS runtimes in parity was the core pain — an ongoing maintenance burden and a source of subtle bugs. It was also confusing for plug developers.
* **Make *server mode* the only mode** (thin client, the server does everything). Rejected: defeats offline-first and the run-anywhere goal, and keeps the product tied to an always-available, more capable backend.
